title: Two-exciton bound states in the Merrifield exciton model
authors: Ning Wu, Runtian Li, Dazhi Xu
abstract: Understanding the formation and dynamics of two-exciton bound states (BSs) is crucial for harnessing multi-exciton phenomena and designing next-generation organic semiconductor materials. While various mechanisms such as intermolecular exciton-exciton interactions or multi-level intramolecular configurations can generate these BSs, a fundamental understanding of their underlying lattice dynamics remains a key challenge. Within this context, the Merrifield exciton model stands out as a premier framework for capturing the intricate quantum mixing between single-site doubly-excited states and two-particle scattering continuum. In this work, by constructing a set of exact two-exciton Bloch states and applying a plane-wave ansatz to treat the resulting inhomogeneous tridiagonal matrices, we provide a complete, rigorous solution to the two-exciton problem in a finite-size Merrifield chain. We analytically map the parameter regions that support two-exciton BSs, proving that at most two distinct types of BSs can emerge, located either above or below the scattering continuum. Furthermore, we provide a quantitative interpretation of how these two types of BSs evolve as a function of the total wave number within the whole Brillouin zone. The obtained closed-form expressions for the eigenenergies and wave functions offer valuable benchmarks for exploring exciton dynamics and optical responses in related molecular aggregates.
summary: This paper rigorously solves the two-exciton problem within the Merrifield exciton model for a 1D chain. By constructing exact Bloch states, the authors prove the existence of at most two types of bound states and analytically map the parameter regimes where these states appear. This work offers crucial benchmarks for understanding multi-exciton dynamics in organic semiconductors.
main_problem: The study aims to understand the formation and dynamics of two-exciton bound states (BSs) in organic semiconductors, which is crucial for designing next-generation materials.
main_result: The authors provide a rigorous solution proving that at most two distinct types of two-exciton bound states (f-type and ee-type) can exist in the Merrifield chain, and they map the parameter regions supporting these states.
method: The research involves constructing exact two-exciton Bloch states and applying a plane-wave ansatz to solve the resulting inhomogeneous tridiagonal matrices derived from the two-exciton Hamiltonian.
model_or_system: The system is modeled by the Merrifield exciton model applied to a finite-size one-dimensional molecular crystal. The Hamiltonian describes the interaction between single-site doubly-excited states and the two-particle scattering continuum.
key_observables: Two-exciton bound state eigenenergies and wave functions, characterized by their spatial distribution (f-type vs. ee-type).
important_parameters: Coupling strengths ($J_1, J_2, J_3$), site energies ($\varepsilon_1, \varepsilon_2$), and the total wave number ($k$) across the Brillouin zone.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes periodic boundary conditions and utilizes a plane-wave ansatz for the solution; the model is idealized by neglecting exciton-phonon coupling.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the level structure of the model, the phase diagram showing BS occurrence based on coupling parameters ($J_2, J_3, 	ilde{\epsilon}$), and trajectories showing how BS properties evolve as the wave number $k$ changes.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical problem, develops the mathematical framework using Bloch states and plane-wave ansatz, analyzes the phase diagram to determine existence conditions for BSs, and finally maps the evolution of these BSs across the entire Brillouin zone.
why_interesting: The rigorous analytical solution and mapping of the parameter space provide deep insights into many-body localization and correlation effects in low-dimensional quantum materials, which is highly relevant to AMO physics and open quantum systems.
